submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE (0.00638%) at Sb 0.654, close to ZnSb2O6 trirutile stoichiometry (MEGNet HSE gap ~1.97 eV, below the 2.1 eV photon energy). Measured EQE peaks near that composition on the Sb-rich side: 0.00069% at Sb 0.22 and 0.0050% at Sb 0.75.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.00069%, ~10x lower; Zn7Sb2O12 spinel region
Measured EQE 0.0050%, lower than idx 15; more Sb-rich past the ZnSb2O6 stoichiometry

consultations.verdict: MEGNet HSE gaps: ZnSb2O6 trirutile 1.97 eV (just below 2.1 eV photons -> absorbing), Zn7Sb2O12 1.95 eV, ZnSb2O4 4.2 eV (non-absorbing), Sb-rich Sb3ZnO7 ~0 (metallic, unreliable). Supports measuring near ZnSb2O6 stoichiometry (idx 15, Sb 0.654) as a stable, absorbing semiconductor.

MACE: Zn7Sb2O12 spinel essentially on hull (0.012 eV/atom), so idx 0 (Sb 0.22, exact stoichiometry) should be phase-pure; with MEGNet gap ~1.95 eV it can absorb 2.1 eV light. Supports measuring as the contrasting end of the line.

MEGNet gives ~0.05 eV for hypothetical ZnSb4O9 (Sb 0.8) — likely an artefact for a hypothetical structure, weakly informative; Sb-rich side may have narrower-gap mixed-valence Sb oxide absorbing 2.1 eV light. Combined with measured trend (EQE rises 10x from Sb 0.22 to 0.65) and GP UCB, supports probing Sb-rich idx 19 (Sb 0.75).
